channel.title: The RigSight log
channel.description: Notes from building RigSight, a free PC monitor for Windows.

item.title: Should RigSight be rewritten in Rust? I measured first
item.description: RigSight felt slow to open, and I wondered whether parts of it should be rewritten in Rust. Measuring every part said no. The slow parts were drivers, Windows and the way the window started, and fixing those made it open in about 1.1 seconds instead of 1.9.

item.title: Taskbar tiles worked on my taskbar, not on theirs
item.description: A GitHub issue asked for more colourful taskbar readings. RigSight 1.2.0 gave every reading a tile and a look of its own, and a bug report 94 minutes later showed a fallback I had never told anyone about.

item.title: Bringing AI back, with rules this time
item.description: Nine days after removing Riggy, I started on a real AI helper. Before writing any of it, I wrote down what it would never be allowed to do.

item.title: Teaching crashes to say how sure they are
item.description: Every crash now says what most likely caused it and how sure that is. Getting there meant one big feature, and cutting most of the next one.

item.title: Making RigSight work without admin rights
item.description: On a standard Windows account RigSight asked for an admin password at every start and recorded nothing without one. Here's how it learned to do what it can, and say what it can't.

item.title: The tests said 15 milliseconds. The app froze.
item.description: Switching pages felt slow, but every test passed. Made-up history was too tidy to show the problem. Real history showed it at once.

item.title: The driver update that knocked RigSight out
item.description: An NVIDIA driver update crashed RigSight's recorder ten seconds after the new driver started, and nothing brought it back.

item.title: Three ways my temperature chart was lying
item.description: Peaks that moved every second, a 74° high that never showed on the line, and a gap that looked exactly like a cool PC.

item.title: Riggy, the helper I shipped and removed two days later
item.description: The first try at letting you ask RigSight questions. It was clever, it was careful, and it wasn't really AI. So it went.

item.title: Bugs that make no noise
item.description: Internet use that silently stopped being recorded, an app 'updated' 45 minutes early, and a game 'installed' ten minutes into a 55 GB download.

item.title: My PC wasn't losing power in its sleep
item.description: RigSight said my PC kept losing power while asleep. It didn't. I had misread a number in Windows' own crash record.

item.title: How light is light? Measuring an app that never closes
item.description: Someone suggested rewriting RigSight's sensor reading in C++. Measuring first showed where the time really goes, and that I had read the wrong memory number.

item.title: The day RigSight told me my healthy fan was clogged
item.description: A warning that compared a resting PC with a gaming one, and the rule it left behind. Compare like with like, or say nothing.

item.title: Getting numbers inside a fullscreen game
item.description: Why a normal window can't draw over some games, how RivaTuner gets around it, and the see-through panel that turned solid black.

item.title: Day one, and 25 versions before midnight
item.description: The first public day of RigSight, what it set out to do, and the first mistake it shipped, which counted the page file as RAM.
